CHIEF COMPLAINT
Bilateral knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 62-year-old male presenting with bilateral knee pain that developed over the weekend while moving boxes up and down basement stairs. The patient reports pain in both knees equally, with onset attributed to repetitive activity and the weight of the boxes. He has a past history of knee problems. The pain was significant enough to disrupt sleep on Saturday night. He has attempted management with Tylenol and ice with minimal relief. Denies any specific injury to either knee.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headaches, or fatigue. Denies weight gain. Reports occasional elbow pain but notes this is nothing out of the ordinary. Recent transplant checks with Dr. Gutierrez a couple of weeks ago were unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- Kidney transplant (several years ago for polycystic kidneys)
- Hypothyroidism
- Arthritis

MEDICATIONS
- Synthroid for hypothyroidism
- Immunosuppressive medications for kidney transplant
- Acetaminophen as needed for pain

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient recently engaged in moving boxes up and down basement stairs over the weekend.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs stable, afebrile, with normal heart rate and blood pressure. Heart examination reveals a 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, which is stable and has been appreciated on prior exams. Knee examination demonstrates edema and erythema of the right knee with pain to palpation and decreased range of motion. Left knee appears normal without significant findings.

RESULTS
Right knee x-ray shows good bony alignment with no acute fracture. Laboratory results show white blood cell count not elevated and kidney function very good. Autoimmune panel ordered. Thyroid panel ordered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Bilateral knee pain/acute exacerbation of arthritis: Prescribed Ultram 50 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain. Advised to take it easy. Autoimmune panel ordered. If symptoms continue, will pursue further imaging and referral to physical therapy.

2. Hypothyroidism: Continue Synthroid. Thyroid panel ordered.

3. Arthritis: Continue current management. Limited by kidney transplant status as patient cannot tolerate certain anti-inflammatory medications. Reassess in a couple of weeks and refer to physical therapy if needed.
